profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.subtitle: Schedules and DNS filters that get assigned to devices
profiles.empty_help: Assign a profile to a device from its detail page to make the schedule and filter take effect.
profiles.id_help: Lowercase letters, digits, hyphen. Used in URLs; cannot be changed after creation.
profiles.description_placeholder: What this profile does (shown on the device page)
profiles.schedule_help: When devices on this profile lose internet. LAN and admin UI keep working.
profiles.blocklists_help: Comma-separated blocklist names (e.g. ads, trackers). The lists themselves arrive in M11.
profiles.builtin_locked: Built-in profile — schedule and filters editable, but cannot be deleted.
profiles.err_id_format: Lowercase letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore (1-64)

device.profile_help: Applies the schedule and DNS filter to this device.

devices.title: Devices
devices.subtitle: Every device that has ever joined this network
devices.empty_help: Devices will appear here once they connect to the Wi-Fi and get a DHCP lease.
devices.stale_help: Device hasn't answered ARP for over 30 days. Likely won't reconnect with this MAC (iOS/Android rotate private MACs). Safe to remove via "Forget device".
devices.display_name_help: Only visible to you in this admin UI. The device itself doesn't see it.
devices.forget_help: Removes the entry from the list. Useful for duplicates created by iOS/Android private-MAC randomization, where one phone shows up under several MACs over time. If the same MAC reconnects, the entry comes back automatically.
devices.forget_online_error: Device is online — wait for it to disconnect first

auth.not_configured: Device hasn't been set up yet

setup.title: Welcome to KnotOS
setup.subtitle: Let's get your device set up
setup.detect_router_available: Both extender and full-router options are available. You'll pick the role on the next step.
setup.detect_no_eth: No USB-Ethernet adapter detected. If you want full-router mode, plug one in and click "Re-probe". Without one, KnotOS will run as a Wi-Fi extender.
setup.detect_timeout: Hardware probe didn't respond. You can continue — KnotOS will run as a Wi-Fi extender — or click "Re-probe" in a few seconds.
setup.role_section_subtitle: KnotOS can run as a Wi-Fi repeater or as a full router with wired internet — we detected a USB-Ethernet adapter, so both options are available.
setup.role_extender_help: Join an existing home Wi-Fi network and broadcast a separate one from this device. No cables needed.
setup.role_router_help: Internet comes in over a USB-Ethernet cable; KnotOS broadcasts its own Wi-Fi network.
setup.wan_section_subtitle: Which interface faces the internet (it will be the one we ask for a DHCP lease on, from your modem or main router).
setup.wan_none_detected: No USB-Ethernet adapter detected. Plug one in, then go Back → Next to re-probe.
setup.channel_help: 1, 6, 11 are the cleanest in most residential areas. Pick whichever is least crowded with your neighbours' networks.
setup.review_warn_router: After applying, "{setup}" disappears and "{ap}" comes up. Internet comes via {wan} — make sure the cable is plugged in.
setup.device_name_help: Used as hostname and {name}.local on the LAN
setup.country_help: Two-letter code, e.g. RU, US, DE
setup.uplink_section_subtitle: The network KnotOS connects to. On a Zero 2W its channel will also be used by your broadcast network.
setup.ap_section_subtitle: Network your devices will connect to
setup.ap_password_help: Leave empty for an open network, otherwise minimum 8 characters
setup.band_help: Only 2.4 GHz is supported on Zero 2W
setup.review_warn: After applying, "{setup}" disappears and "{ap}" comes up on the same channel as {uplink}. Reconnect to "{ap}" and sign in with your admin password.
setup.err_password_short: Password must be at least 8 characters
setup.err_uplink_psk: Password is required for secured networks
setup.err_ap_psk: Wi-Fi password must be at least 8 characters (or empty)

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.subtitle: Optional features that extend KnotOS
plugins.empty_help: Plugins live under /usr/lib/knot/plugins/. Restart knotd after installing one to discover it.
plugins.v01_note: v0.1 plugins are metadata only. Runtime ships in v0.2.

system.title: System
system.subtitle: Manage your device
system.shutdown_confirm: Shut down? You'll need physical access to power it back on.
system.factory_reset_warn: Wipes settings and re-runs the setup wizard. Current passwords and Wi-Fi configs will be lost.
system.update_subtitle: Upload a new knotd binary to update without re-flashing

security.subtitle: Local root certificate that signs the admin UI's TLS cert. Install it on your devices once and the browser will stop warning about an "unsafe connection".
security.regenerate_confirm: Re-issue the leaf? The root stays the same, so trust copies installed on your devices remain valid. The browser may ask you to reconnect right after.
security.install_help: On iOS and macOS you also need to enable the root in Trusted Root Certificates (Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings). On Android, install through Settings → Security → Advanced → Encryption & credentials → Install from SD card.

protection.title: Protection
protection.subtitle: DNS-level ad and tracker blocking, scoped per device and profile
protection.refresh_queued: Blocklist refresh started in the background
protection.top_blocked_empty: Nothing has been blocked yet — browse a bit and stats will appear here.
protection.sources_empty: Lists haven't loaded yet. They'll appear within a minute of startup, or hit "Refresh lists".
protection.upstream_subtitle: Where knotd forwards queries that aren't blocked. DoH hides domain names from your ISP and from on-path censoring middleboxes.
protection.upstream_mode_udp_help: Plain DNS over UDP/53. Fast, but your ISP sees every query in cleartext.
protection.upstream_mode_doh_help: RFC 8484: queries ride a TLS tunnel to /dns-query. The ISP sees only the TLS handshake to Cloudflare/Quad9.
protection.upstream_list_help_udp: One per line as host:port. Empty falls back to Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 + Google 8.8.8.8.
protection.upstream_list_help_doh: Full https:// URLs ending in /dns-query. Empty falls back to Cloudflare + Quad9.
protection.queries_empty: No queries yet. As devices resolve domains, they'll show up here.
protection.disabled_help: Protection turns on once the device leaves setup mode and enters Wi-Fi extender role. Come back here once setup is finished.

updates.subtitle: Fetch a fresh knotd binary from GitHub Releases, verified with an Ed25519 signature. Atomic replace, automatic service restart.
updates.signing_off: This build was compiled without a release key — signature checks are off. Don't use in production.
updates.apply_confirm: Install version {version}? The binary will be downloaded, signature-verified, atomically replaced, and knotd restarted. Your session survives.
updates.manual_help: Developer-only: uploads a locally-built knotd without signature verification. For normal updates, use the /system/update/apply path above.
updates.disabled: Auto-update is disabled in this build (no signing key, or dev mode).
updates.error_timeout: GitHub did not respond in time. Check the device's internet and try again.
updates.error_github: Could not reach GitHub. Make sure the Pi has internet access.

rescue.subtitle: Per-device Ed25519 key. A knotd binary signed by this key is accepted even if the upstream release key has been compromised. The private half is shown exactly once — save it somewhere safe.
rescue.reveal_confirm: Reveal the private key? This is irreversible — after the click the key is wiped from the device, only your copy remains. If you lose it you'll need to re-flash to generate a new one.
rescue.warning_one_shot: Once you click, the private key disappears from the device forever. Save it immediately.
rescue.already_revealed_help: The private key has been delivered. Only the public half remains here. To regenerate, delete /etc/knot/rescue.json and restart knotd.
rescue.error_already_revealed: Private key was already revealed earlier.

vpn.title: VPN server
vpn.subtitle: WireGuard road-warrior — reach your home LAN from anywhere by scanning a QR. Per-peer profiles work the same as on the LAN: ad-block + schedules travel with you.
vpn.endpoint_help: Either a DDNS hostname (no-ip, Cloudflare, duckdns) or a public IP. Whatever you set ends up in every peer's client config — no endpoint, no incoming connections.
vpn.peers_empty: No peers yet. Click "Add peer" to issue a config for your phone / laptop.
vpn.full_tunnel_help: On: everything from the peer goes through home (more private, slower on the road). Off: only LAN-bound traffic uses the VPN.
vpn.remove_confirm: Remove peer "{name}"? Its old QR will stop working.
vpn.delivery_help: Open the WireGuard app on the peer device, tap "+" → "Scan from QR code" and point the camera at the screen. Tunnel is up in a second.
vpn.delivery_warning: The private key is shown ONCE. Close this dialog and it's gone forever. If lost, delete the peer and create a new one.
vpn.disabled: VPN endpoints are disabled in this build.

guests.title: Guest network
guests.subtitle: Time-limited Wi-Fi with a one-time password and QR. Guests reach the internet but are walled off from your main LAN.
guests.empty_help: Spin up a temporary guest network — knotd generates the password and draws a QR. Your guest scans it with their phone camera and connects in one tap. The network disappears on its own when the timer runs out.
guests.ssid_help: Up to 32 characters. Empty defaults to your main SSID + «-guest».
guests.revoke_confirm: Close the guest network right now? Connected guests will lose Wi-Fi instantly.
guests.isolation_help: Guests can't see your main LAN devices — internet only. Separate subnet, separate DHCP scope, drop on forwarding between guest and LAN.
guests.disabled: Guest network requires Wi-Fi router mode on Pi 4/5 with USB Ethernet, or a Zero 2W with a multi-BSS-capable Wi-Fi driver.
